The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

Daisy and the Dance That Went Sideways

Daisy had planned a dance for Everybody Day. She drew three little steps on a paper leaf. Forward, together, bow. She knew the steps so well she could do them carrying a pea on her head.

She taught it to Crab, who was visiting from the pond. “Forward,” she called. Crab went sideways. “Together.” Crab went farther sideways. “Bow!” Crab vanished behind a flowerpot.

“I’ll show you very slowly,” Daisy said. She lifted one foot and held it in the air. Crab lifted a foot. Then another. He had plenty left. Daisy wobbled and sat down on the pea.

Crab looked out from behind his pot. “Would you like to learn the step I keep doing?” Daisy rubbed her bottom. Teaching had turned out quite lumpy. She might as well have a go at learning.

“Think of going through a narrow crack,” Crab said. Daisy turned sideways. “Now let the wind push you.” Daisy slid one foot. The other followed. To her great surprise, the flowerpot sailed slowly past her nose.

Bella joined in with a hop. Chip added a turn. When they got back to the first pot, Crab stopped. Daisy bowed. That step fitted the new dance beautifully. Everybody bowed to everybody else.

Daisy turned her paper leaf over. On the back she drew Crab’s sideways tracks. She hung it on the Welcome Tree by one corner. Depending on the breeze, you could learn two different dances.

Crab asked about the pea trick. Daisy brought another pea. Crab carried it sideways all the way home. Nobody could say where his head ended and his shoulders began, but the pea stayed on splendidly.

Read together

Which step would you invent for this dance?
